name: Santiago Luna
event: UFC Fight Night: Procházka vs. Stirling
summary: A 22-year-old bantamweight from Tijuana ('Border Boy', Entram Gym; 8-1, 2-1 UFC), born in San Diego and a three-time national Greco-Roman champion (Wikipedia). Took two of his three UFC fights as a late replacement: an R1 KO of Quang Le on under two weeks' notice, and a fight with Bryce Mitchell that he lost by arm-triangle eight seconds from the end. In between he beat Angel Pacheco 30-27 x3.

how_they_fight.Striking: Fast, with knees and body hooks as his main weapons; Cageside notes an 'obvious speed advantage' in the pocket against Pacheco and his 'patented knee' (he ended that fight with a flying knee). Floored Quang Le with a left hook; our data has two knockdowns in that fight. About 3.4 significant strikes a minute and he absorbs only 2.4. Our data has him out-landing Pacheco 131-56.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Wrestler with submissions: four submission wins (R1, R1, R2, R3) on the regional scene. 5 of 5 takedowns against Pacheco in our data, and a jumping guillotine in R3 (Cageside). Threatened a d'arce against Mitchell. Gets back up quickly from bottom (Pacheco).
how_they_fight.Defense: Takedown defense is about 59%. Mitchell took him down twice, reversed him repeatedly and held him for 700 seconds in our data, taking the back and mount before the R3 arm-triangle (4:52). Le buckled him early with a punch and a head kick (Cageside). Never stopped by strikes.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Seven stoppage wins: four in R1, one in R2, two in R3 (both regional). His decision over Pacheco was strongest in R3 against a tired opponent (Cageside). His one loss came at the very end of R3 after being controlled for most of the fight, and he started R3 aggressively with a takedown, so no clear fade, but he gives up position late in scrambles.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Aggressive and willing to scramble; young and still learning. Gave up his back in R3 against Mitchell while hunting a finish (Cageside).

patterns: Knees and body hooks in the pocket, with speed
Two of three UFC fights on short notice
Finishes come at any point: four R1, one R2, two R3
concerns: Bottom position and scrambles against a strong top grappler (Mitchell)
Low takedown defense number for a wrestler
keys_to_beat: Win the clinch and get on top; ride him rather than scramble
Make him strike at range, away from his knees
Watch the neck when shooting on him

news.text: Booked against Aleksandre Topuria on the Qatar card; his first UFC fight with a full camp since February.
Lost to Bryce Mitchell by arm-triangle at 4:52 of R3, on short notice replacing Victor Henry. First pro loss.
